provenance_note: The gate criteria g1-g5 and every sweep were fixed in src/run_synthetic.py BEFORE it was executed. These manifest files transcribe them and were written after the run, so they are a faithful record rather than an independent pre-registration. Stated plainly rather than implied.
question: for the same person, do anatomically corresponding LEFT and RIGHT bones become more consistent at the correct candidate focal, and does that improve a scene-anchored focal estimate?

naive_formulation_rejected.what: compare the FIXED reference 3D bone lengths of the two hands
naive_formulation_rejected.why_rejected: that value does not depend on the candidate focal, so d/df = 0 and it carries no focal information. Measured range over a +-50 % sweep: exactly 0.

primary_formulation.name: CANDIDATE_CONDITIONED_SHARED_BONE_FIT
primary_formulation.per_candidate_focal: refit one sequence-shared bone-proportion vector per side from that side's own 2D, with free per-frame pose
primary_formulation.loss: L_bilateral(f) = mean |l_L(f) - l_R(f)| over corresponding bones
primary_formulation.scale: both vectors sum to 1, so absolute hand size is never used as a cue and a person with larger hands is not penalised
primary_formulation.symmetry: NOT enforced as a hard equality; real people are not perfectly symmetric. A side-scale nuisance r_LR would be redundant once both vectors are sum-normalised, so it is not introduced.
primary_formulation.linearity: with bone directions fixed the hand is linear in the bone-length vector, so the fit alternates PnP for pose with a linear solve for the lengths
primary_formulation.initialisation: uniform. The reference bone lengths are never used as an initial value or a prior centre.

articulation_source: OTHER_CAMERA_ONLY_REFERENCE_3D bone DIRECTIONS only; the reference bone LENGTHS are deliberately not fixed, otherwise the hypothesis could not be tested
overfitting_guard: deterministic alternating FIT / EVAL frame split; the bone vector is estimated on FIT frames and the reprojection is also measured on held-out EVAL frames

focal_grid.definition: q = f / f_scene (real) or f / f_true (synthetic)

synthetic_gate.g1: the bilateral objective must not be focal-invariant
synthetic_gate.g2: in the noiseless moderate-perspective condition the true focal must be near the minimum (median focal error <= 5 %)
synthetic_gate.g3: held-out reprojection must identify the focal
synthetic_gate.g5: the fixed-length control must be flat
synthetic_gate.rule: g1 and g2 and g4 are required. If the gate fails, the GigaHands real-data phase is NOT run.

forbidden: GT focal as an optimisation input
target camera inside the reference articulation
frame or hand filtering by focal performance
